review_scope: Ten complete UI protection reusable fragments read as inert pinned evidence. No native bypass performed; version applicability and omission certification remain separate.

claims.statement: The pinned fragment labels UI file-upload protection public preview and subject to change; it is not a current-release guarantee.
The blocking assertion requires a supported secret and a repository secured by push protection.
The UI presents the secret location and underlines the secret; this documentation does not prove that any target UI was inspected.
A test-only or false-positive bypass reason closes the generated alert without notification; closed state alone does not verify that classification.
The fix-later classification keeps the alert open and notifies the commit author and repository administrators; permission to push is not remediation.
Bypass email to organization owners, security managers, and repository administrators depends on their opting in, so recipient absence is not evidence of no bypass.
The three presented reasons are test-only, false-positive, and fix-later; these are contributor classifications rather than independent secret-safety decisions.
Within the user-protection feature condition, a bypass reason is required when repository secret scanning is enabled.
User protection covers supported secrets in public repositories without repository secret scanning, but allowing the secret requires no reason and creates no alert in that described mode.
A request comment explains claimed safety or context; it is not reviewer approval or a verified safety attestation.
Submitting the request is distinct from approval and from a successful push.
The procedure directs the requester to check email for a response; no actual mailbox or delivery receipt was examined.
Review completion is documented to trigger a decision email; notification does not itself establish an approved decision.
